messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Generating a large mesh with holes - performance issues?
parts:
Hi,
A mesh of the entire notrh Atlantic with ~1 km resolution will be very large, in particular if the polygon has small details making the boundary have small segments. Try increasing the max.edge values and cutoff by a factor 100, and then gradually decrease it.

For the islands, the barrier method is often a better alternative than making a mesh with holes.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Generating a large mesh with holes - performance issues?
parts:
Whether polygons are treated as holes or as "inverted holes" is
determined by the winding order. The convention in fmesher is that
"inside is to the left" when walking along the polygon boundary. That
means that a counterclockwise order is a regular domain boundary,
whereas clockwise order creates a hole. The sf standard essentially
works like that as well (but the sf package does not, as it often
calls the "libproj" library that has the opposite convention, and sf
neglects to convert back to the sf standard definition. So in practice
one may need some experimentation to get the intended behaviour). But
for the barrier method, you _don't_ want the islands to create holes;
you may just want the triangle edges to follow the island coastlines,
which can be achieved by specifying them using the "interior" argument
in the mesh creation.

Finn
